meta.title: Aero: publish a prototype, test it, get findings
meta.desc: Put a Claude, Figma or HTML prototype online, send one test link, and get recordings, transcripts and what to fix first. Free to start.
p1.h1: From an idea you had today
to findings you can show your team

hero.aria: How Aero works, a 50-second loop. In Claude, Aero’s one prompt is pasted and Claude publishes Pocket to pocket.aeroapp.ai. In Aero the site is live, and its own tab opens. From the site’s menu, “User test this site” creates a test with its own link. On Maya’s own computer she opens the link, allows the microphone and the tab, and tries two tasks while her tab and voice are recorded. Back in Aero her session is transcribed with friction points, and Insights puts every session together: what to fix first, with quotes. The Publish, Test and Review buttons jump to each step; pressing the step that is playing pauses it.
pub.h2: Start from an idea, a link or a Figma file
pub.body: Describe it in a prompt and build it in Claude or ChatGPT, then paste Aero’s prompt into the same chat. It’s published at its own aeroapp.ai address, with nothing to install.
pub.more: Already have a Figma prototype link, or an HTML file, folder or zip? Add that instead. Publish again to the same address whenever it changes.

pr.h2: Priced for one designer, not a corporate
pr.body: Free to start, recordings included. Paid plans have a 7-day free trial, are billed monthly, and need no call or contract.
faq.items: Do my testers need an account or an app?
No. They open the link in their browser on their own computer, allow the microphone and the tab, and start. You choose who gets the link.
The browser tab with your prototype, and the tester’s voice as they think aloud. Not their camera and not their other tabs.
How does one prompt publish my site?
Aero gives you a prompt with a key in it. Paste it into the Claude or ChatGPT chat where you built the thing and it sends the files to Aero. Nothing to install or connect.
A Claude artifact or anything you built in a chat, a Figma prototype link, or an HTML file, folder or zip.
How soon is the transcript ready?
About a minute after each session ends, with a short summary and the friction points in the tester’s own words.
Is the test link the same as my site’s?
No. Testing a site makes a copy with its own short link, so you can change the test without touching the live site.
Can I use my own domain?
Yes, on Solo and up. Password protection comes with Basic and up.
Can people test on a phone?
Figma prototype tests work on a phone and record the tester’s voice only. Site and HTML tests need a computer, because Aero records the tab.
What do I get for free?
3 test sessions with recordings, transcripts and summaries, and sites that stay live for 7 days. Paid plans have a 7-day free trial.

hero.aria.classic: How Aero works, a 50-second loop. In Claude, Aero’s one prompt is pasted and Claude publishes Pocket to pocket.aeroapp.ai. In Aero the site is live; Visit opens it in a new tab. From the site’s menu, “User test this site” creates a test with its own link, which is copied and sent to six testers in a WhatsApp group. On Maya’s own computer the message arrives; she opens the link, allows the microphone and the tab, and tries two tasks while her tab and voice are recorded. Back in Aero her session is transcribed with friction points, and Insights sums up every session. Then the owner starts a new site and copies the prompt again. The Publish, Test and Review buttons jump to each step; pressing the step that is playing pauses it.
